target.title: fix(google-meet): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in local audio bridge
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers for Google Meet command audio bridge child streams
- stop the bridge through the existing failure path when primary audio input/output streams error
- cover agent and realtime bridge stream errors with focused regressions
- collision check: no open PR found for the Google Meet local audio bridge stream-error issue or `extensions/google-meet/src/realtime.ts`

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/google-meet/index.test.ts -t "stops the Chrome agent audio bridge|stops the Chrome realtime audio bridge|pipes Chrome command-pair audio through the realtime provider"` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests passed, 100 skipped

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Google Meet local command audio bridges listened for stdout/stderr `data` events but did not handle readable stream `error` events, so an `EPIPE` from those streams could surface as an unhandled error instead of closing the bridge.
Real environment tested: mocked Google Meet command bridge child processes using Node `PassThrough` streams in Vitest; no live Google Meet session or real audio device required.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: emitted `error` on mocked input stdout, input stderr, output stderr, and stale output stderr streams during the focused bridge tests.
Evidence after fix: the emitted stream errors did not throw out of band; the bridge logged the existing warning path, closed the bridge, closed the provider session, and terminated the child processes with `SIGTERM`.
Observed result after fix: local audio stream failures are contained by the bridge stop path instead of becoming unhandled stream errors.
What was not tested: full CI and live Chrome/Google Meet audio capture/playback with real devices.
